scope.focus: historical visual perception, adaptive routing, Retina artifact consumption, native-vision supersession and relevance to current FRANK v0.1 user-adaptive Micro Visual Classifier requirements
scope.non_overlap: Cross-reads the existing Drive Digital Retina learning lineage and adds the distinct Project-Frankenstein routing/backend lineage. It does not claim full Project-Frankenstein tree/history enumeration.

chronology.event: Project-Frankenstein introduced a two-stage Adaptive Visual Pipeline: fast YOLO+OCR/scene heuristics first, then local VLM escalation when a hand-composed confidence score fell below a gate or the question required richer understanding.

The prior frank_visual_pipeline.py and frank_adaptive_vision.py were explicitly deleted/replaced by FrankEye, which fused Retina v8 CNN, DINOv2 features, OCR, face detection and other local visual features.

Screenshot-specific vision was repaired; the commit records removal of useless CIFAR-10 classification for screenshots and cleanup of misleading CIFAR/DINOv2 output, preserving a concrete negative result about indiscriminate classifier surfacing.

Native Qwen3.5 multimodal vision was added. At frozen head, tools/native_vision.py states that it replaces FrankEye for native image understanding, while FrankEye remains in the repository as an older/parallel implementation artifact.

Frozen-head VCB executable code imports tools.native_vision, despite an internal class comment still referring to FrankEye. This is documentation/supersession drift, not evidence that both backends are simultaneously authoritative.

mechanism_findings.finding: The February Adaptive Visual Pipeline was adaptive in routing, not in user-specific learning: it combined detector/OCR/scene evidence with a hand-authored confidence score and escalated to a VLM when confidence was below 0.55 or task semantics demanded deeper interpretation.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Reusable-with-adaptation as a cost/uncertainty routing ancestor for the current familiar-fast-path/deeper-perception architecture; it is not itself the current Micro Visual Classifier.

mechanism_findings.finding: Frozen-head FrankEye loads Retina v8 weights from an external ~/projects/retina/cache/retina_v8.pt path and defines configuration specifically for compatibility with retina.py, establishing a concrete Project-Frankenstein -> Digital Retina artifact dependency.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Feature/classifier artifacts require explicit backbone/version/provenance identity and migration/invalidation rules in H1/H2/UDB rather than implicit filesystem coupling.

mechanism_findings.finding: Frozen-head VCB persists prose visual descriptions and log-correlation observations into world_experience, but does not persist user-scoped visual prototypes, trusted example tiers, candidate classifier states or open-set calibration state.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Visual description memory and adaptive familiarity memory are distinct data products and should remain explicitly separated in the current architecture.

mechanism_findings.finding: The visual backend changed from heuristic detector+VLM routing to FrankEye and then toward Qwen3.5 native multimodal vision within roughly five weeks.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: The current learner should expose a backend-neutral familiarity/open-set contract with explicit feature-backbone compatibility instead of binding semantic identity to one visual backend.

cross_source_reconciliation.finding: The Drive Digital Retina lineage contains the stronger historical learning ancestor: learned K-means/prototype-like dictionaries, replay/miss iteration and measured threshold/FPR behavior. Project-Frankenstein contributes the separate adaptive routing/backend-integration lineage. They should not be collapsed into one historical mechanism.

Project-Frankenstein FrankEye consumed an external Retina v8 weight artifact, connecting the repositories operationally even though the Project-Frankenstein head does not contain the Retina training source.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.result: CIFAR-10 classification was removed for screenshots after producing useless/garbage visual output.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.lesson: A classifier can be locally confident yet task-irrelevant; fast-path gating must be calibrated to the actual domain/task and preserve escalation.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.result: The historical term 'adaptive' referred to heuristic compute routing. No versioned per-user prototypes, GOLD/SILVER admission, candidate-vs-current promotion, rollback or explicit open-set state were found in this implementation.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.lesson: Do not count adaptive routing as adaptive learning or as satisfaction of the current FRANK v0.1 MVC contract.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.result: A class comment says VCB uses FrankEye while executable code imports NativeVision.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.lesson: Backend identity must come from executable/versioned configuration and receipts; comments/docs can drift across rapid supersession.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.result: The code claims that about 90% of images do not need VLM, but this run found no retrieved benchmark receipt establishing that claim.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.lesson: Treat performance comments as hypotheses until backed by measured workload-specific receipts.

current_inheritance.inherit: Fuse the Drive Retina prototype/dictionary learning ancestor with Project-Frankenstein's fast-first/deep-on-uncertainty routing pattern. Keep the MVC as familiarity/routing only, not sensor truth.
Expose backend_version, feature_backbone_version, classifier/prototype_version, calibration identity, evidence tier, open-set result, compute path and escalation reason in replayable receipts.

Persist visual sensor evidence, prose descriptions, familiarity prototypes/classifiers and training-example provenance as related but non-conflated objects with explicit supersession and compatibility edges.
Represent fast-path/deep-path decisions as deterministic typed transitions over confidence/open-set/resource state; do not bake a specific CNN/DINO/VLM backend into the semantic contract.

reject_or_adapt: Do not reuse the historical hand-composed confidence <0.55 threshold as semantic authority or as a current calibrated open-set gate.
Do not interpret detector/OCR routing adaptation as evidence of user-specific learning.
Do not treat prose VLM descriptions or BRONZE/self-generated labels as autonomous training truth.
Do not bind the new MVC to CIFAR-10 classes or to one historical FrankEye backend.
Do not treat the historical '~90% VLM saved' code comment as a measured fact.
Do not let a native multimodal VLM replacement erase the fixed FRANK v0.1 requirement for a small user-adaptive familiarity learner.
cheap_discriminating_tests: Replay the same recurring-user and OOD image sequence through a historical-style heuristic escalator and MVC-0 prototype routing; compare task correctness, unknown rejection, escalation rate and compute cost.
Train/collect MVC state on one frozen feature backbone, then change backbone version and assert explicit invalidation or validated migration rather than silent prototype reuse.
Use screenshot near-neighbors and unrelated CIFAR-like classes to verify that locally confident but task-irrelevant classifier output cannot enter KNOWN_HIGH_CONFIDENCE fast path.
Crash between candidate evaluation and promotion; assert last-known-good classifier/prototype version is restored and the same replay yields identical state transitions.
Feed native-VLM prose descriptions back as BRONZE examples and require autonomous training admission rejection unless independently promoted to trusted provenance.

branch_feedback.frank: DELTA: preserve fast-first/deep-on-uncertainty routing, but pair it with the separate learned prototype lineage and current provenance/open-set/rollback laws.
branch_feedback.harness: DELTA: add backend-supersession, feature-version invalidation and task-irrelevant-confidence regression tests to MVC acceptance.
branch_feedback.claycode: DELTA: adaptive visual semantics should be backend-neutral typed state transitions with explicit compatibility/version identities.
branch_feedback.claygraph: DELTA: represent sensor evidence, description memory, prototype/classifier state and backend supersession as distinct linked nodes/edges.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: DELTA: persist feature-backbone compatibility and visual learner version lineage independently of prose visual observations.
branch_feedback.gwt: NO_CHANGE: this lineage does not establish a new workspace ignition/broadcast mechanism.
branch_feedback.emergenz: NO_CHANGE: routing/backend evolution is architectural history, not new causal-emergence evidence.
branch_feedback.hyperposition: NO_CHANGE: no new higher-order set-valued coupling result is established by this shard.
branch_feedback.clayresearch: DELTA: dissolved Retina should combine learned familiarity with selective deeper perception while keeping both non-authoritative relative to sensor/effect evidence.
branch_feedback.q12_index: DELTA: Project-Frankenstein contributes a distinct adaptive-routing/backend-supersession ancestor that complements, rather than duplicates, the Drive learned-dictionary lineage.

earned_work.reason: Reusable routing and backend-migration mechanisms were recovered, but row-level historical earned-work deduplication remains incomplete and must not double-credit the already mapped Drive Retina lineage.

level0_effect.reason: Project-Frankenstein exact frozen tree/history denominator remains unfrozen because the current connector has no recursive read-tree/archive/clone surface. This is valid semantic/history evidence, not repository-wide denominator closure.

promotion.reason: Historical mechanism, supersession and negative-result evidence was preserved. No new live implementation result was produced and Level-0 remains open.
